name: event-registry-python (NewsAPI.ai / Event Registry SDK)
what_it_holds: Official Python SDK for the Event Registry news-event API: article/blog search by keyword, concept, topic, source, sentiment, date; event clustering; trending-concept queries; articles ranked by social shares. MIT, 203 commits.
why_useful: Event-level (not just article-level) news aggregation could support an events/shocks feed (gap #11) or a regulation-news tracker (gap #12) if Airbnb/STR terms are queried, though free tier is capped at last 30 days and requires an API key.

name: newspaper3k / newspaper4k
what_it_holds: Python library for full-text article and metadata extraction (text, authors, date, images, keywords) from arbitrary news URLs, with parallel multi-threaded downloading; 35+ languages. MIT/Apache-2.0 dual license, 670 commits.
why_useful: Generic extraction backend that would sit behind a Skift/PhocusWire/regulatory-news crawl once target URLs are identified (e.g. via waybackpy or a sitemap) -- turns raw HTML into structured article records for a text corpus.
themes: News and event databases: GDELT tooling, Google News scrapers, travel-industry news datasets (Skift, PhocusWire), regulatory news trackers

name: tomslee/airbnb-data-collection
what_it_holds: Tom Slee's original Airbnb scraper (Python 3 + PostgreSQL/PostGIS), predecessor to Inside Airbnb. 488 stars, 184 forks, 250 commits, last substantive activity ~2019 (MIT license, no longer maintained by author). The repo itself has no committed CSVs (schema/scraper only), but it was used to run quarterly-ish 'surveys' of listings across dozens of cities from 2014-07 to ~2017 (one example city shows 18 survey snapshots May 2014-Jul 2017). The author's own site (tomslee.net/airbnb-data-collection-get-the-data) hosts the resulting CSV exports by year (2014, 2015, 2016, 2017) as a direct download, and several Kaggle mirrors of 'Tom Slee Airbnb data' exist. Combined with the code here, this is a fully reproducible listing-level, multi-year, multi-city panel that predates Inside Airbnb's own coverage.
why_useful: Directly fills gap #1 (historical/archived STR dumps pre-2023) with a source 5-8+ years older than our current earliest coverage; also a second, independent scrape methodology (not Inside Airbnb's own tool) so could crosscheck listing-count/price levels for 2015-2017 in cities we still care about (e.g. NYC, LA, Paris, London, Barcelona).
last_activity: archived/no longer maintained per author (author announcement 2017; repo still on GitHub)
geography: dozens of global cities (bounding-box + city surveys)
size_hint: code repo is small; bulk data lives externally on tomslee.net, size unknown, described as 'get the data' bulk downloads
